title: 1954 AHSME Problem 39
statement: The locus of the midpoint of a line segment that is drawn from a given external point \(P\) to a given circle with center \(O\) and radius \(r,\) is:

answerChoices.label: C
answerChoices.text: a circle with center \(P\) and radius \(r\)

answerChoices.label: D
answerChoices.text:
a circle with center at the midpoint of \(\overline{PO}\) and
radius \(2r\)

answerChoices.label: E
answerChoices.text:
a circle with center at the midpoint of
\(\overline{PO}\) and radius \(\dfrac12r\)

solutions.text:
As the endpoint \(X\) moves on the circle centered at \(O,\) its midpoint \(M\) with the fixed point \(P\) is the image of \(X\) under a dilation of scale \(\frac{1}{2}\) centered at \(P.\) Therefore the locus is a circle whose center is the midpoint of \(\overline{PO}\) and whose radius is \(\frac{r}{2}.\)

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: Let the variable endpoint on the given circle be \(X\) and its midpoint with \(P\) be \(M\)
The map \(X\mapsto M\) is a dilation centered at \(P\) with scale factor \(\frac{1}{2}\)
